subject: Voyager AI — Redwood SDK connector & co-sell planning
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex@voyagerai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + Redwood SDK connector possibility

Hi Soojin,

Quick intro — I run partnerships at Voyager AI. We build an orchestration layer that lets ISVs and platforms stitch multiple open models and toolchains together. A few of our larger customers are asking for a first-class integration with Redwood so they can pick Redwood as a serving backend from Voyager UI and get telemetry + cost insights out of the box.

Would Redwood be open to a lightweight connector (OAuth + runtime routing + a small tracing shim)? We imagine a launch that includes:
- Auth flow guide and sample creds for a test account
- A runtime connector that maps Voyager model calls to Redwood’s /v1/generate API and preserves trace ids
- A short co-marketing plan and a joint demo for two pilot customers

I attached a rough API spec and a proposed MVP SOW with timelines. If this sounds interesting, can we get 30 minutes next week for a tech + GTM sync?

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Head of Partnerships, Voyager AI
[Attachment: Voyager-API-Spec.pdf (pdf)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@voyagerai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + Redwood SDK connector possibility

Alex — thanks for the intro and the materials. This is right in our sweet spot.

High-level thoughts:
- Technical: runtime connector + trace propagation is feasible; we'll need a small adapter in Voyager to translate their call metadata into Redwood routing keys and propagate a Redwood-trace header. Karthik, can you review the attached API spec and flag any breaking gaps?
- Security: we'll want to confirm token exchange patterns and scopes; Ben, can you pick this up?
- GTM: co-demo + one joint pilot sounds good. Marissa — please propose a pilot customer profile and a 4–6 week success metric set (SLOs, cost delta, latency targets).

We can do a 30-min sync next Wed (10/14) at 10am PT. Alex — does that work?

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
[Redwood Inference — redwood.ai]

Subject: Re: Intro + Redwood SDK connector possibility

Alex / team —

Thanks for sharing the spec. A couple practical questions up front so we can scope the pilot cleanly:

1) Auth & scoping
- Do you expect per-tenant tokens (recommended) or a single shared service account for the initial pilot?

2) Model selection & fallbacks
- Will Voyager surface specific Redwood model names (e.g., redwood/rtd-large-quant) or generic capabilities (text-generation)? We want to preserve canary/fallback rules in routing.

3) Telemetry & traces
- What trace context does Voyager include today? We prefer passing a single X-Redwood-Trace header and an optional user-op-id. If Voyager has existing trace IDs, we can map them to ours.

4) Data handling
- Any PII concerns for pilot customers? If so, we should enable strict retention/ingress limits and provide a private test instance.

Assignees: Karthik — api compatibility + adapter effort estimate; Ben — security/token flow + minimal checklist; Soojin — GTM plan and pilot customer shortlist.

I sketched a 6-week timeline in the attached SOW that covers integration, staging, and a joint demo. Alex — can you confirm availability for Wed 10/14 10am PT (same slot)?

—Marissa

Marissa Cole
Head of ISV Partnerships | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-mvp-sow-Redwood-Voyager-v1.docx]

From: Alex Chen <alex@voyagerai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Voyager Partnerships <partner-success@voyagerai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + Redwood SDK connector possibility

Thanks all — Wed 10/14 10am PT works for our lead engineer and me (we're in PST as well). Quick replies to your questions:

1) Auth: per-tenant tokens preferred; we can implement an initial service-account path for the POC but will need per-tenant in staging.

2) Model names: Voyager currently surfaces capability-level selectors; we can add an optional mapping table to surface Redwood model ids if needed. We'll start capability-first and add explicit model mapping for the pilot customers who want pinning.

3) Traces: Voyager uses a trace_id (hex) and span_id fields internally. We can emit those in an X-Voyager-Trace header; happy to map to X-Redwood-Trace on our side if that's easiest.

4) PII: pilot customers will be enterprise with moderate controls — we should plan a private Redwood staging instance with reduced retention.

Attaching the API spec (updated) and a short diagram of the auth flow. Look forward to the sync.

—Alex

[Attachment: Voyager-API-Spec.pdf (updated)]
